domain: hydrological risk operations - river-station alert-threshold exceedance prediction (Colombia, IDEAM automatic-station telemetry)
prediction_question: HYPOTHESIS under test: given a Colombian river station's hourly maximum-level telemetry through hour H (raw automatic-sensor readings, published openly on datos.gov.co), predict whether the water level will exceed the station's official alert threshold within the next 48 hours. A useful prediction feeds municipal early-warning (IDEAM/Carabineros/SNGRD protocols) with lead time for evacuation and road closures. The exact missing fact: an official per-station alert/danger threshold in machine-readable form - without it the label degrades to a self-referential percentile, which is a different (weaker) task.
prediction_time: Telemetry is hourly and near-real-time on the live feed; the published dataset is one current table of raw unvalidated sensor values (publisher clause: 'los datos ... no han sido validados por el IDEAM'), and IDEAM documents a preliminary -> en revision -> definitivo lifecycle for its validated series (separate 'Niveles Horarios' dataset). UNRESOLVED: the as-of policy - current raw values may later be corrected, so features computed from today's table may differ from what the live feed showed at the time; construction must either use only the raw-feed table (accepting and measuring the revision effect) or obtain vintage information. This is the main open question besides the threshold.
target_definition: PROPOSED (blocked on threshold source): binary - station-hour (or station-day) level exceedance of the official alert threshold within (H, H+48]. Label source: valorobservado hourly maxima (cm/m) per station; the threshold would come from an official IDEAM table (NOT FOUND in the bounded probe: the station catalog cqmv-a99d has no threshold columns, and a catalog search for alert-level datasets returned nothing machine-readable). Fallback (weaker): per-station seasonal high-quantile exceedance - requires a known-event fixture (e.g. a documented 2021-2025 flood on a specific river) before that route may be probed further.

sources.name: Nivel Maximo del Rio (hourly max level per automatic station)
sources.api: Socrata, anonymous. Measured 2026-10-23: 14,672,316 rows (SoQL count), span 2001-01-01T07:17 .. 2026-10-21T23:59, 345 distinct stations. Columns: codigoestacion, codigosensor, fechaobservacion, valorobservado, nombreestacion, departamento, municipio, zonahidrografica, latitud, longitud, descripcionsensor, unidadmedida. Rows/year measured: 2009: 844,095; 2017: 1,214,445; 2019: 1,547,326; 2022: 446,478; 2025: 1,219,800; 2026 (partial): 991,988. Sample unit measured 'mt' (Nivel Maximo sensor). Publisher clauses in the description: raw, unvalidated, published under Ley 1712 de 2014.

measurements.probe_2026_10_23: Socrata metadata + SoQL (scripts in session scratch): rows 14,672,316; span 2001-01-01..2026-10-21; 345 stations; rows-by-year listed in sources; sample rows show hourly 'Nivel Maximo' in metres with station/department/municipio/zona metadata; catalog has no threshold columns; catalog v1 search for alert-threshold datasets returned no machine-readable result.
measurements.capacity_note: Volume is ample for station-hour exceedance pairs across 26 years, but positive counts are NOT measured until a threshold exists - no base-rate or split claim is made yet.

next_action: Next probe (bounded, one session): (1) locate the official per-station alert/danger threshold: search datos.gov.co catalogue API for 'nivel de alerta'/'umbral' datasets, IDEAM's SAIC flood-warning pages and geoportal, and IDEAM's published station 'niveles de alerta' PDFs; if only PDF, extract for the subset of stations with clean telemetry and record the fixture; (2) measure per-station continuity (gap rates) and exceedance base rates on one bounded window (e.g. 2019-2024) against the threshold; (3) resolve the raw-vs-validated as-of policy: compare a fixed station-month in the raw table against the validated 'Niveles Horarios' (ig79-2jr9) family if vintages permit; (4) re-verdict: ready if threshold + base rates + as-of policy resolve; drop if no official threshold is obtainable in any form (the percentile fallback requires a known-event fixture and is a weaker task - decide explicitly then).
